a: OOP organizes code into objects bundling data and behavior. Core ideas: classes, encapsulation, inheritance, polymorphism.
A tree is nodes with children. A binary search tree keeps smaller values left and larger right, so lookups take about O(log n).
Dynamic programming solves big problems by saving answers to repeated subproblems (memoization), like caching fibonacci results.
A library is code you call when you want. A framework calls your code and gives you the structure, like React, Django or Express.
Binary uses only 0 and 1. Each place is a power of 2, so 1011 is 8+2+1 = 11.

q: what is a bit and byte
a: A bit is a single 0 or 1. A byte is 8 bits and can store a value from 0 to 255.
RAM is fast short-term memory for running programs. Storage (SSD or HDD) is slower long-term memory that keeps files when power is off.
The CPU handles general tasks in sequence very fast. The GPU has thousands of small cores that do many simple calculations at once, great for graphics and AI.
An SSD has no moving parts and is much faster, quieter and more durable. An HDD is cheaper per gigabyte.
Ethernet is a cable and is faster and more stable. Wi-Fi is wireless and convenient but can be slower and less reliable.
An IP address identifies a device on a network. A VPN encrypts your traffic and routes it through another server, hiding your IP from sites.

q: how to speed up my computer
a: Restart, close heavy apps and browser tabs, uninstall unused programs, check startup apps, keep 15 percent of the disk free, and update the system. An SSD upgrade helps most.

q: how to speed up my phone
a: Restart it, clear app caches, delete unused apps and big videos, back up photos to the cloud, and keep the system updated.
5G is the newest mobile network, much faster with lower delay than 4G, but coverage is still growing.
iPhone is simple, polished and long supported. Android offers more choice, customization and price range. Both are great, so pick the ecosystem you already use.
